segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: Welcome to Harbor Voices. Today we look at the clock on the harbor office wall, which has been wrong since 1962.

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.body: It stopped during a storm, and the council voted to leave it, so every ferry timetable carries a small note about it.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: Is it true that visitors set their watches by it anyway?

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.body: Every summer. We find them on the quay an hour early, or eleven hours late, depending on how you count.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: And the harbor master has never asked for it to be repaired?

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.body: Never. She says a clock that is right twice a day is more than most committees manage.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: Does the mechanism still work at all?

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.body: It is fine. I wound it myself in March, and it ran for a week before anyone noticed and complained.

segments.speaker: Mara
segments.body: So the wrong time is now the official time.

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.body: Only on the quay. Out past the breakwater we use the tide, which has not been wrong yet.
